summary: The precision alpha's pointwise apparent-place reduction is, as far as an independent chain can tell, correct to the model it claims: against a chain I wrote from scratch with pyerfa 2.0.1.5 + jplephem over the same DE440s (200 epochs 1852-2148 x 10 bodies, matched conventions: light-time with target at emission and barycentric observer at reception, eraLd with finite-distance q, eraAb with the observer's barycentric v/c, pfw06/fw2m with nut00b adjusted to P03, ecliptic via epsA+deps), the alpha agrees to 4.2-5.0e-7 arcsec on every planet and the Sun (that constant is exactly the documented omission of ERFA's Klioner potential term in eraAb) and to 1.34e-5 arcsec on the Moon, the latter being double-precision noise from cancelling two 1.5e8 km EMB vectors at two epochs, not a model deviation. TDB-TT (three terms, not two as the docs say) is within 21.8 us of eraDtdb over 20,001 epochs (claim <30 us holds); nut00b, its P03 adjustment, pfw06, obl06 and the NPB matrix reproduce pyerfa to 7e-12 arcsec / 2.2e-16; 2000A-minus-2000B is 0.00215 arcsec max on the corpus (tree says <=0.0025, confirmed). The interval machinery is sound in every family I attacked (60,000-case exact-rational fuzz of the primitives: zero containment failures; Clenshaw forward error at most 6.4 per cent of the 4n^2u allowance over 3,102 exact evaluations; record-boundary selection correct at every one-ulp probe) but several allowances are covered by slack rather than by the stated analysis: a derived nutation-argument constant whose formation rounding exceeds the 8u pad by 1.51x, tau evaluated at 1+2.2e-16 at record starts for packs with non-integer epochs, and an unpadded Lipschitz constant. The two things that matter most for exceeding Swiss in this dimension: (1) Mars-outward bodies are planetary-system barycentres (Jupiter 0.071, Saturn 0.053, Pluto 0.093 arcsec off the physical centre, measured from NAIF satellite kernels and confirmed against Horizons 599/5 and 999/9 to 0.3 mas), and Swiss CAN return centres given its sepm*.se1 files while the alpha cannot at all; (2) the alpha offers none of Swiss's variants (topocentric, heliocentric, barycentric, J2000/astrometric, sidereal, apparent rates) and no output carries a sky-referenced error bound, so the 'rigorous bounds on every output' path is unbuilt. Re-measured on a fresh 2,000-row corpus, alpha vs Swiss(.se1) is 0.0104 arcsec max (Moon) / 0.00041 p50, and the decomposition shows the Moon residual is U-shaped around the LLR era (a DE431-vs-DE440 lunar-orbit signature, refining the tree's 'grows backwards' hypothesis) while Pluto's residual is 0.895-correlated with Swiss's own nutation departure from IAU 2000B: the alpha's reduction is more than three orders of magnitude closer to the IAU/ERFA chain than Swiss is. One harness premise failed: Swiss cannot read SPK/DAF .bsp files, so swe.set_jpl_file('de440s.bsp') silently returns Moshier (flag 4), and no Swiss-with-DE440s isolation is possible on this machine.

findings.title: Outer planets are system barycentres, up to 0.093 arcsec off the physical centre; Swiss can return centres, the alpha cannot
findings.claim: For Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto the alpha returns the planetary-system barycentre (ephemeris.mjs BARYCENTRE_NOT_CENTRE, honestly flagged) with no path to the body centre. Measured from the NAIF satellite kernels the centre-vs-barycentre offset in apparent geocentric position reaches Jupiter 0.0709" (p50 0.0186", offset 219.6 km), Saturn 0.0529" (p50 0.0303", 311.4 km), Neptune 0.0035", Pluto 0.0934" total (0.0829" lon / 0.0862" lat, 2132 km). Swiss Ephemeris returns the same barycentres by default but offers SEFLG_CENTER_BODY, which with its planetary-moon files (sepm9599/9699/9999.se1) returns the centre; on this machine the flag fails with 'SwissEph file sepm9599.se1 not found', which proves the capability exists and that plain calls are barycentres. This is a concrete accuracy item where Swiss (with its data) beats the alpha by up to 0.09" on Pluto and 0.07" on Jupiter, i.e. 7-9 times the alpha's 0.0104" residual against Swiss.
findings.evidence: R/examples/precision-alpha/src/core/ephemeris.mjs:366-373 (BARYCENTRE_NOT_CENTRE), reduce.mjs:41-42,68. S/centre/sat-offsets.py -> S/centre/sat-offsets.json (3,000 epochs per body inside each kernel's coverage intersected with 1850-2150; 7.4 s). Horizons arbiter check at JD 2460000.0 TT: 599-minus-5 dlon +0.0018" dlat +0.0004", 999-minus-9 dlon -0.0706" dlat +0.0436" (S/horizons/q-{599,5,999,9}-2460000.txt, queries in the .query files) vs my kernel-derived +0.0018/+0.0001 and -0.0703/+0.0437. Swiss flag test S/centre/swiss-centre.py -> swiss-centre.json: plain calc flags 258 (SWIEPH), FLG_CENTER_BODY raises the missing-sepm-file error for Jupiter/Saturn/Pluto and is a no-op for Mars. Consistent with the committed numerics track (docs/platform/evidence/precision-2026-09-20/numerics/RESULTS.md section 4, B2: Jupiter <=0.0767", Pluto <=0.0935" proven).
findings.reproduction: cd S/centre && ../venv/bin/python sat-offsets.py; python3.11 swiss-centre.py (pyswisseph 2.10.03, ephe path <swisslab>/ephe).
findings.impact: Within the alpha's own domain this is the largest known systematic against the sky for Jupiter, Saturn and Pluto, and it is invisible to any Swiss-default comparison because Swiss shares the convention. A stack that wants to be more accurate than Swiss must return centres; Swiss already can.
findings.fix: Compile a compact centre-relative-to-barycentre Chebyshev series per planet from the NAIF satellite kernels (jup365/sat441 or the 348/480 files present) into the pack as a 'sun'-style delta frame (the offset is a smooth few-hundred-km quasi-periodic function; 8 coefficients per 4-day record over 300 years is about 2.6 MB per planet, far below the 313 MB the numerics track feared), apply it at the emission epoch exactly as reduce.mjs's offsetKm hook already does, set isSystemBarycentre false, and add the kernel-derived offset to the tier-b tests. For dates outside satellite-kernel coverage keep the barycentre and say so per result.

findings.title: No topocentric, heliocentric, barycentric, J2000/astrometric, sidereal or rate output: Swiss offers all of them
findings.claim: The alpha's contract is a single quantity: apparent geocentric ecliptic longitude/latitude of date plus a light-time-corrected distance (reduce.mjs CONTRACT.coordinates, notModelled). It reports no apparent angular rate (CONTRACT.velocities), no topocentric place (no geodetic observer, no diurnal aberration), no heliocentric or barycentric place (barycentric position is deliberately excluded, CONTRACT.barycentricPositionExcluded), no J2000/astrometric/true-position variants outside the experimental fixed-frame search modes, and no sidereal longitudes. Swiss provides each through flags (FLG_TOPOCTR with geodetic observer and altitude, FLG_HELCTR, FLG_BARYCTR, FLG_J2000, FLG_TRUEPOS, FLG_NOABERR, FLG_NOGDEFL, FLG_SIDEREAL, FLG_SPEED with speeds consistent with the apparent chain). Every chart-level consumer (houses need the apparent obliquity and sidereal time, station finding needs rates, a birth chart needs the topocentric Moon at the 1-arcsec level of parallax) is therefore outside the alpha today.
findings.evidence: R/examples/precision-alpha/src/core/reduce.mjs:39-90 (CONTRACT), README.md 'What it supports, exactly'. Swiss flags exist and answer with .se1 data on this machine (swiss-centre.json shows FLG_SPEED honoured; FLG_TOPOCTR etc. are documented Swiss features, not measured here). The interval modules already carry the derivatives needed for rates (aberration.mjs aberrateInterval PDot, deflection.mjs deflectInterval DDot, frame-of-date.mjs Rdot).
findings.reproduction: Read CONTRACT in reduce.mjs; grep -n 'topocentric\|heliocentric\|sidereal' R/examples/precision-alpha/src/core/*.mjs returns only notModelled entries.
findings.impact: Keeps the stack materially below Swiss in capability even where its geocentric numbers are better. Lunar topocentric parallax alone is up to ~1 degree; ignoring it is not an option for a birth chart that claims to exceed Swiss.
findings.fix: Add to the Reducer: (a) an observer model (WGS84 geodetic to GCRS via eraGd2gc-equivalent, Earth rotation via ERA/GAST from the same IAU 2006/2000B chain, polar motion optional) giving a topocentric observer position and velocity, with diurnal aberration falling out of using the observer's total barycentric velocity; (b) analytic apparent rates by differentiating the pointwise chain (the derivative formulas already exist in the interval modules; port them to point form); (c) heliocentric/barycentric/astrometric/J2000 variants as switches on the existing stages; (d) sidereal by subtracting an ayanamsa computed from the same frame chain. Validate each against pyerfa (atco13-style topocentric) and Swiss flags as instruments.

findings.title: Interval allowances are covered by slack, not by the stated analysis, in three places (no counterexample found)
findings.claim: (a) frame-of-date.mjs forms the combined nutation arguments ARG_A[j], ARG_B[j] as double sums of five products and then pads them RELATIVE TO THE RESULT (I.iv / I.scale, 8u); for a cancelling sum the formation error exceeds that pad. Exact-rational check: term j=23 (multipliers [1,0,2,-2,2], A = -86773.3098") has formation error 1.164e-10" against a pad of 7.71e-11" (ratio 1.51), leaving 3.9e-11" = 1.9e-16 rad of argument uncovered; ARG_B worst ratio is 0.20. Containment survives only because sinCosInterval's ABS_ERR (4e-15) has room, and the module comment attributes that room to a different rounding. (b) Ephemeris.raw()/seriesAt() promise |tau| <= 1 after the record-selection fix, but for a pack whose initEt/intervalSec are not integers the computed tau at a record start is -1.0000000000000002 (reproduced at 6 of 7 edges of a synthetic pack); |T_k| then exceeds 1 by about k^2 * 2.2e-16, which is inside clenshawRoundoff's 4n^2u only because that allowance is generous (measured worst actual Clenshaw error is 6.35 per cent of it). (c) seriesBounds uses sum|d_k| of the floating-point derivative() coefficients as the Lipschitz constant with no pad; measured under-statement is at most 6.98e-17 relative (below u), again absorbed by the roundoff term. The interval primitives themselves (add, sub, mul, div, scale, sqrt, norm) passed a 60,000-case exact-rational containment fuzz with zero failures, and the 4n^2u Clenshaw bound held with 16x margin over 3,102 exact evaluations across five coefficient families including tau = 1+ulp.
findings.evidence: R/examples/precision-alpha/src/core/frame-of-date.mjs:118-131 (ARG_A/ARG_B), 164-174 (the comment about what covers the rounding); ephemeris.mjs:233-251 (record selection, tau); cheb.mjs:45-55 (derivative), 86-90 (clenshawRoundoff), retarded.mjs:147-159 (mean-value enclosure using bnd.maxAbsFirst unpadded). Artifacts: S/enclosures/argb-rounding.mjs and interval-fuzz.mjs (ARG_A worst term JSON in the output), boundary.mjs (tau = -1.0000000000000002 at 6 edges; plain floor() wrong at 3/10 probes, the while-loops correct it; one ulp past the last inclusive end refused), clenshaw-bound2.mjs (worst ratio 6.350e-2; derivative understatement 6.976e-17; (n-1)/2 growth claim verified for n = 8, 20, 32, 64).
findings.reproduction: cd S/enclosures && node interval-fuzz.mjs && node argb-rounding.mjs && node boundary.mjs && node clenshaw-bound2.mjs (each under 2 s).
findings.impact: Not a wrong answer today: no input interval was found whose enclosure excludes the true value, in seven families tried (primitive ops with exact rationals; derived-constant formation; record-boundary tau; Clenshaw with all-ones, alternating, random, geometric and ephemeris-like coefficients at tau = +-1, +-(1-1e-12), 1+ulp; sinCos quadrant boundaries via the tree's own BigInt test; mean-value half-width construction). But a completeness theorem whose padding is right by luck is weaker than Swiss's plain numbers only in the sense that it claims more; the claim should be made true by construction.
findings.fix: Pad ARG_A/ARG_B by an absolute allowance equal to 5u times the sum of |multiplier * constant| (the term magnitudes, not the result), or compute them once as exact rationals and store the double plus its residual; in ephemeris.mjs clamp the computed tau into [-1, 1] only when the record has already been proven to contain et (and document that the residual is a tau-rounding term of at most 2u); add an explicit tau-argument term n^2 * u * sum|c| and a (n/2) u relative pad on sum|d_k| to the cheb.mjs analysis so the allowance is justified rather than measured. Add the two exact-rational scripts as tier-A tests.

findings.title: Five documentation statements in the core contradict the code or each other
findings.claim: (1) reduce.mjs:244-248 says ERFA's eraLdsun clamp 'silently caps the deflection at roughly a tenth of an arcsecond'; deflection.mjs:70-75 measures the actual peak under dlim=1e-6 at 5.7586" and says the reduce.mjs comment is wrong but leaves it. (2) CONTRACT.coordinates calls distKm 'the geometric geocentric distance' while reduce.mjs:230-231 returns |target(emission) - observer(reception)|, the light-time-corrected distance (the quantity Swiss also returns; the label is what is wrong). (3) CONTRACT.corrections and TIME_MODEL call TDB-TT a 'two-term' form; tdbMinusTt has three terms (0.001658 sin g + 0.000014 sin 2g + 0.0000224 sin(L-LJ)). (4) trig.mjs:170 states the cosine truncation term as (pi/4)^20/20! <= 4e-21; the polynomial stops at z^8 = r^16 so the first omitted term is (pi/4)^18/18! = 2.0e-18 (still 2,000x under ABS_ERR). (5) trig.mjs:196 says PIO2_HI has its 'low 33 bits clear'; 0x3FF921FB54400000 has 22 trailing zero bits (fdlibm's 'first 33 bits of pi/2' means 33 significant bits); exactness of k*PIO2_HI for |k| <= 5 holds either way. Also CONTRACT.notModelled omits the Shapiro delay, which deflection.mjs's profile does list.
findings.evidence: File:line references above; the TDB-TT term count is visible in reduce.mjs:149-153 and frame-of-date.mjs:413-418; cos polynomial coefficients trig.mjs:248-256 end at 1/16! = 4.7794773323873853e-14.
findings.reproduction: Read the cited lines; for (4) compute (Math.PI/4)**18/6.402373705728e15.
findings.impact: None on numbers; each one misleads a reviewer of the error analysis, and (1) understates a 5.8" effect by a factor of 58 in the shipped reducer's own comment.
findings.fix: Correct the five comments/labels and add 'Shapiro delay (<= ~2e-4 s of light-time, < 1e-7 arcsec)' to CONTRACT.notModelled.

findings.title: Reduction order and conventions match the ERFA apparent-place chain to 4.4e-7 arcsec (planets) with only the documented Klioner term missing
findings.claim: Order is BCRS geometric -> Newtonian light-time (target at emission, barycentric observer at reception; reduce.mjs:215-229) -> eraLd with e = observer - Sun(reception), em at reception, q = target(emission) - Sun(emission) (reduce.mjs:237-254, the eraLd argument semantics) -> eraAb form with the observer's BARYCENTRIC velocity (EMB + Earth-rel-EMB analytic derivative, reduce.mjs:209-213) and bm1 = sqrt(1-v^2) but without ERFA's w2 = SRS/s potential term -> frame bias + IAU 2006 precession + IAU 2000B/P03 nutation as one fw2m matrix whose gamb/psib carry the bias once (frames.mjs:100-110) -> ecliptic via epsA + deps. Against an independent pyerfa + jplephem chain over the same DE440s (200 epochs x 10 bodies) the max separation is 4.37e-7" (Sun), 4.17-5.02e-7" (planets) and 1.34e-5" (Moon); the planetary constant is the omitted w2 term (ERFA bounds it at ~0.4 uas), and the Moon figure is rounding noise from EMB cancellation (finding 8), with light-time agreeing to 8e-9 s and distances to 2.7e-5 km. The frame bias direction is verified by the matrix match to eraFw2m(pfw06 + nut00b/P03) at 2.2e-16 and to eraPnm06a at 1.0e-8 rad (= the 2000A/2000B difference).
findings.evidence: S/erfa-chain/dump-alpha.mjs (Reducer over tools/spk-backend.mjs, raw DE440s), S/erfa-chain/erfa-chain.py -> erfa-chain-results.json (2.3 s). Reader agreement Spk2 vs jplephem: Moon-rel-EMB 4.7e-7 km, EMB 1.4e-5 km, Sun 6.8e-9 km (S/erfa-chain/dump-spk2.mjs).
findings.impact: The pointwise reduction is not what stands between the alpha and 'most accurate available'; the data (finding 1) and the missing variants (finding 2) are. This measurement should replace 'documented at 0.0107" against Swiss' as the statement of the reduction's correctness, since the 0.0107 is dominated by the instrument.
findings.fix: Add the optional Klioner w2 term (aberration.mjs already has withPotential) to reduce.mjs's 'full' aberration, and commit this ERFA-chain comparison as a tier-b test so the 4e-7" figure becomes a regression gate.

findings.title: TDB-TT three-term form is within 21.8 us of eraDtdb; a full series would remove the last time-scale term
findings.claim: tdbMinusTt (reduce.mjs:149-153) differs from ERFA's eraDtdb (Fairhead & Bretagnon, geocentric u=v=0) by at most 2.181e-5 s, rms 6.2e-6 s, over 20,001 epochs 1850-2150, so the '<30 us' claim holds. At the Moon's 0.55"/s this is at most 1.2e-5" of longitude, comparable to the Moon's numerical floor (finding 8) and the only remaining model-side term above 1e-6" for the Moon.
findings.evidence: S/erfa-chain/erfa-chain.py output: 'TDB-TT: alpha 3-term vs eraDtdb, n=20001: max |diff| 2.181e-05 s rms 6.212e-06 s'.
findings.impact: Opportunity: Swiss's handling of TDB-TT was not measured here; ERFA-level (sub-us) time scale is cheap and would make the Moon's time argument better than any 30-us convention.
findings.fix: Port the 787-term eraDtdb series or its 20-term truncation (error ~1 us) into reduce.mjs and frame-of-date.mjs (the interval version needs the same terms as sine intervals; reducedRadians already handles this).

findings.title: IAU 2000A would move longitudes by at most 0.00215 arcsec on the corpus; Swiss uses 2000B by default too
findings.claim: nut00b matches erfa.nut00b to 6.7e-12" (dpsi) / 1.2e-12" (deps) over 601 epochs 1850-2150; adjustToP03 is bit-for-bit eraNut06a's fj2/0.4697e-6 rule. Replacing 2000B/P03 with eraNut06a (2000A) changes apparent longitude by 0.00215" max on the 2,000-row corpus, 0.00225" max in dpsi over the grid, rms 0.00074". The tree's <=0.0025" is confirmed. Swiss's own nutation departs from published 2000B by up to 0.00153" on the same rows (Pluto residual vs Swiss is 0.895-correlated with that departure), so 2000A is a step past Swiss, not a step to it.
findings.evidence: S/erfa-chain/erfa-chain-results.json 'frames' and '2000A minus 2000B' lines; S/swiss/ decomposition output (dpsi diff max 0.00153").
findings.reproduction: erfa-chain.py frame block; S/swiss/swiss-vs-alpha.py then the decomposition snippet in the transcript.
findings.impact: 2 mas is below the centre/barycentre item by 40x and below the lunar-series item by 5x; worth doing after those, when nutation becomes the limiting term (the numerics track says the same).
findings.fix: Carry the already-parsed 1,365-term table (docs/platform/evidence/precision-2026-09-20/numerics/src/nutation-series.json) behind a nutation:'2000a' switch; cost measured there at 77 us per evaluation.

findings.title: Geocentric Moon is formed by cancelling two 1.5e8 km barycentric vectors at two epochs: a 1.3e-5 arcsec numerical floor
findings.claim: Reducer.apparent computes geo = [EMB(et-tau) + MoonRelEMB(et-tau)] - [EMB(et) + EarthRelEMB(et)] in doubles (reduce.mjs:209-229 via backend.state). The EMB terms are at different epochs so they do not cancel algebraically, and their rounding (1.4e-5 km, i.e. 1e-13 relative on 1.5e8 km) does not cancel numerically; against an independent reader/chain the Moon shows 1.34e-5" and 2.45e-5 km worst, 40 of 200 epochs above 1e-6", while planets sit at 4e-7". The EMRAT derivation itself is right: the pack stores Moon relative to EMB (segment 301/3) and Earth = EMB - MoonRelEMB/EMRAT (compile.mjs:357-364, ephemeris.mjs:350-351), EMRAT is taken from the coefficient ratio and verified over every coefficient, and the validated search merges the weights so the geocentric Moon is one series with weight 1 + 1/EMRAT (validated-search.mjs:112-137) rather than two independent errors added.
findings.evidence: S/erfa-chain/erfa-chain-results.json (per-body worst), S/erfa-chain/dump-spk2.mjs reader comparison (EMB 1.437e-5 km, Moon 4.657e-7 km).
findings.reproduction: erfa-chain.py, then the Moon-sorting snippet in the transcript.
findings.impact: Irrelevant against Swiss (mas level) but it is the alpha's true Moon precision floor and would cap a future sub-1e-5" claim.
findings.fix: Form the geocentric Moon as MoonRelEMB(et-tau) - EarthRelEMB(et) + [EMB(et-tau) - EMB(et)], computing the bracket from the EMB Chebyshev polynomial difference within a record (or velocity x tau plus a second-order term when tau spans records), which keeps every term at the 4e5 km scale.

findings.title: Re-measured against Swiss on 2,000 fresh rows: 0.0104 arcsec max, and the residual is the instrument, not the reduction
findings.claim: Alpha (raw DE440s) vs Swiss 2.10.03 with sepl_18/semo_18.se1 (flag 258 = SWIEPH confirmed on every call), TT input, 200 epochs 1852-2148 x 10 bodies: |dlon| max 0.01041" (Moon), p50 0.00041", p95 0.00283"; Sun 0.00245, Venus 0.00704 (one 1850-1900 row), Mars 0.00298, Jupiter 0.00188, Pluto 0.00151. Decomposition: the Moon residual is U-shaped, mean -0.0003" in 1950-2000, -0.0049" in 1850-1900 and -0.0070" in 2100-2150 (max 0.0104 at 2100-2150), which is the signature of two lunar ephemerides (Swiss's DE431 fit vs DE440) diverging on both sides of the LLR data span, and REFINES the numerics track's 'grows backwards in time' hypothesis (it grows forwards too). Pluto's residual correlates 0.895 with Swiss's own departure from published IAU 2000B nutation (<=0.00153"), leaving 0.00064"; the Sun's remainder after removing that term is <=0.00145". Since the alpha matches the ERFA chain to 4e-7" on the same data, the alpha's reduction is more than three orders of magnitude closer to the IAU/ERFA chain than Swiss's.
findings.evidence: S/swiss/swiss-vs-alpha.py -> swiss-vs-alpha.json; decomposition output in the transcript (swe.calc ECL_NUT per row). Committed 160-row figure: docs/platform/evidence/precision-2026-09-20/numerics/RESULTS.md headline 0.010730".
findings.impact: Supports the 'exceeds Swiss' claim on the reduction and, if DE440's lunar orbit is the better one (it carries newer LLR), on the Moon by up to 0.01" outside 1950-2000; a DE431 kernel or DE441 Horizons vectors would settle attribution.
findings.fix: Cite this decomposition instead of the bare 0.0107"; test the lunar attribution with two Horizons VECTORS requests (DE441 Moon geocentric, 1850 and 2140) against the pack, which needs no frame conventions.

findings.title: Harness premise failed: Swiss cannot read de440s.bsp; FLG_JPLEPH silently answers with Moshier (flag 4)
findings.claim: swe.set_ephe_path('<swisslab>'); swe.set_jpl_file('de440s.bsp') (or the absolute path) followed by calc(..., FLG_JPLEPH) returns flags 4 (MOSEPH) with no exception; positions then differ from the alpha by up to 2.82" (Pluto), 1.64" (Moon), which is Moshier's accuracy, not a reduction difference. Swiss's JPL reader takes the asc2eph binary format, not SPK/DAF. Consequently the 'Swiss-with-DE440s vs Swiss-with-.se1 isolates the series' and 'Swiss-with-DE440s vs alpha isolates the reduction' experiments proposed to all nine auditors are impossible on this machine, and any auditor who did not read the returned flag has compared against Moshier.
findings.evidence: S/swiss/swiss-vs-alpha.py first block ('returned flags [260]'), and the follow-up probe in the transcript: 'set_jpl_file(de440s.bsp): returned flags 4 -> MOSEPH=True lon=327.9627403' vs se1 327.9627295 vs Moshier-forced 327.9627403 (identical). Also S/centre/swiss-centre.json 'de440s_jpleph' rows carry flags 260.
findings.reproduction: <swisslab>/venv/bin/python -c "import swisseph as swe; swe.set_ephe_path('<swisslab>'); swe.set_jpl_file('de440s.bsp'); print(swe.calc(2451545.0, swe.MARS, swe.FLG_JPLEPH))"
findings.impact: Affects the audit, not the engine: the reduction-vs-series isolation has to be done with pyerfa + jplephem (as here) or with a de440 file in JPL's binary format.
findings.fix: For future measurements obtain JPL's ascii/binary DE440 (linux_p1550p2650.440 via asc2eph) for Swiss, or rely on the ERFA/jplephem chain; add a flag assertion to every Swiss harness script (tools/measure/swiss.py already reads flags).

findings.title: Horizons QUANTITIES=31 is an IAU76/80 ecliptic-of-date frame: 0.049 arcsec from the alpha at J2000 for Mars, so it cannot arbitrate at the mas level
findings.claim: Horizons' legend for ObsEcLon/ObsEcLat says 'IAU76/80 ecliptic-of-date'. At JD 2451545.0 TT Horizons gives Mars 327.9627159 / -1.0677844 while the alpha (IAU 2006/2000B, ICRF bias) gives 327.9627294 / -1.0677946: +0.0487" / -0.0367", the size of the 1976 vs 2006 obliquity constant (84381.448 vs 84381.406 = 0.042") and the FK5/ICRF bias. The site's engine.test.ts JPL gate uses the same quantity; at its 0.05-degree gates that is harmless, but no sub-0.05" claim about the alpha can be made against quantity 31. Horizons remained useful for frame-free differences: 599-vs-5 and 999-vs-9 in the same frame reproduced my kernel-derived centre offsets to 0.3 mas.
findings.evidence: S/horizons/q1-mars-2451545.txt lines 83-86 (legend) and the $$SOE row; alpha value from the node one-liner in the transcript; S/horizons/q-*.query record the exact query strings (5 requests total).
findings.reproduction: curl the query in S/horizons/q1-mars-2451545.query; node one-liner in transcript for the alpha's Mars at ttDays=0.
findings.impact: Prevents a false 'disagrees with JPL by 0.05"' conclusion about the alpha and prevents using q31 as the mas arbiter the audit brief hoped for.
findings.fix: For a mas-level arbiter use Horizons VECTORS (geometric ICRF states, DE441) against the pack, and apparent RA/Dec (quantity 2) only after confirming its precession/nutation model in the legend; keep the ERFA chain as the reduction arbiter.

findings.title: No output carries a sky-referenced error bound; the pointwise apparent() carries none at all
findings.claim: The validated/experimental searches enclose the PACK POLYNOMIAL rigorously but explicitly exclude the pack's proven compression bound ('a pack's own declared bound is not evidence', validated-search.mjs:558-571) and everything external (result.mjs EXTERNAL_UNCERTAINTY), and Reducer.apparent() returns lon/lat/distKm with no uncertainty field. The compiler does prove a fit bound (0.0224 km geocentric, cited in reduce.mjs:70-89) and this audit shows the reduction is within 5e-7" of ERFA, so a per-result bound of the form 'polynomial enclosure + proven fit bound/distance + model-omission budget (Klioner 4e-7", 2000B-vs-2000A 2.3e-3", TDB-TT 1.2e-5" Moon, centre offset for barycentre bodies)' is derivable today. Swiss cannot offer any bound; this is the clearest path to being provably, not just measurably, more accurate.
findings.evidence: validated-search.mjs:543,558-571; result.mjs:191-203; reduce.mjs:288-302 (return shape). Bound inputs: this audit's measurements (findings 1, 5, 6, 7) and docs/platform/evidence/precision-2026-09-20/compiler/RESULTS.md candidate D.
findings.reproduction: Read the cited lines; rt.apparent(...) has no uncertainty key (README usage block).
findings.impact: Without it the 'rigorous proven error bounds on every output' differentiator from Swiss is a property of the search internals, not of anything a chart consumer receives.
findings.fix: Add an `uncertainty` object to apparent(): numerical (Clenshaw + rounding, from cheb.mjs), data (pack's proven fit bound propagated through 1/distance, plus the centre-offset bound for barycentre bodies), and model (the itemised omissions above), each labelled proven/measured/estimated exactly as result.mjs already distinguishes.

measurements.name: Alpha pointwise reduction vs independent pyerfa+jplephem chain on the same DE440s
measurements.method: S/erfa-chain/dump-alpha.mjs runs Reducer(CORRECTED) over tools/spk-backend.mjs at 200 jittered TT epochs 1852-2148 x 10 bodies; S/erfa-chain/erfa-chain.py rebuilds the chain from jplephem states (Earth = EMB + 399/3) with erfa.ld (finite q, dlim 1e-14), erfa.ab (barycentric v/c, bm1), erfa.pfw06/fw2m with erfa.nut00b + P03, ecliptic via epsA+deps; also erfa.nut06a/pnm06a variant.
measurements.result: max sep 1.343e-5" (Moon; EMB rounding), p50 3.46e-7", p95 4.17e-7"; per body: Sun 4.37e-7, Mercury 4.73e-7, Venus 4.96e-7, Mars/Jupiter/Saturn/Uranus/Neptune 4.17-4.19e-7, Pluto 4.17e-7 (= omitted Klioner w2 term); |dtau| <= 7.8e-9 s; |ddist| <= 2.7e-5 km; 2000A-2000B on longitude max 0.00215" rms 0.00074"

measurements.name: TDB-TT three-term form vs eraDtdb
measurements.method: 20,001 epochs 1850-2150 from dump-alpha.mjs, erfa.dtdb(jd, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) in erfa-chain.py
measurements.result: max |diff| 2.181e-5 s, rms 6.21e-6 s; max |TDB-TT| 0.001697 s; claim <30 us holds

measurements.name: Nutation, precession, obliquity and NPB matrix vs pyerfa
measurements.method: 601 epochs t in [-1.5, 1.5] cy; alpha nut00b/adjustToP03/pfw06/meanObliquityArcsec/npbMatrix vs erfa.nut00b (+P03 rule), pfw06, obl06, fw2m, pnm06a
measurements.result: nut00b dpsi 6.7e-12" deps 1.2e-12"; pfw06 2.9e-12"; obl06 0; matrix vs fw2m(2000B/P03) 2.2e-16; vs pnm06a (2000A) 1.0e-8 rad; dpsi(2000A)-dpsi(2000B/P03) max 0.00225"

measurements.name: Spk2 reader (SpkBackend) vs jplephem
measurements.method: S/erfa-chain/dump-spk2.mjs dumps Moon/Earth rel EMB, EMB, Sun, Jupiter states at the 200 epochs; Python compares
measurements.result: max |dpos|: moon 4.66e-7 km, earth 5.7e-9, emb 1.44e-5, sun 6.8e-9, jupiter 6.2e-6 km; velocities <= 2.7e-12 km/s

measurements.name: Centre-vs-barycentre offsets from NAIF satellite kernels
measurements.method: S/centre/sat-offsets.py: jplephem over jup348 (599/5), sat480 (699/6), nep097 (899/8), plu060 (999/9), 3,000 epochs each inside kernel coverage intersected with 1850-2150, offset at emission projected perpendicular to the line of sight and into ecliptic lon/lat

measurements.name: Horizons arbiter for centre offsets and for quantity-31 conventions (5 requests, cached)
measurements.method: QUANTITIES=31, CENTER=500@399, TIME_TYPE=TT, TLIST JD; Mars 499 at 2451545.0; 599, 5, 999, 9 at 2460000.0
measurements.result: 599-5: dlon +0.0018" dlat +0.0004" (kernel-derived +0.0018/+0.0001); 999-9: dlon -0.0706" dlat +0.0436" (kernel -0.0703/+0.0437); Mars J2000: alpha - Horizons = +0.0487" lon, -0.0367" lat, explained by Horizons' IAU76/80 ecliptic-of-date frame

measurements.name: Swiss FLG_CENTER_BODY behaviour
measurements.method: S/centre/swiss-centre.py: pyswisseph 2.10.03, Jupiter/Pluto/Saturn/Mars at 4 epochs, .se1 path and the .bsp 'JPLEPH' path, flags read on every call
measurements.result: .se1 plain flags 258 (SWIEPH); FLG_CENTER_BODY raises 'SwissEph file sepm9599.se1 (9699, 9999) not found' for Jupiter/Saturn/Pluto and is a no-op for Mars; the .bsp path returns flags 260/4 = MOSEPH

measurements.name: Alpha vs Swiss (.se1) on 2,000 fresh rows, with nutation decomposition
measurements.method: S/swiss/swiss-vs-alpha.py: swe.calc TT, FLG_SWIEPH|FLG_SPEED, flags asserted 258; then per-row swe.calc(ECL_NUT) to remove (dpsi_alpha - dpsi_swiss)

measurements.name: Interval primitive containment fuzz and derived-constant padding
measurements.method: S/enclosures/interval-fuzz.mjs: 60,000 random interval pairs across 40 decades, exact BigInt rationals for add/sub/mul/div/scale/sqrt/norm; S/enclosures/argb-rounding.mjs: exact rational ARG_A/ARG_B vs 8u pad
measurements.result: 0 containment failures in 7 x 60,000 checks; ARG_B worst ratio 0.20 (term 41); ARG_A worst ratio 1.51 (term 23, [1,0,2,-2,2], uncovered 3.9e-11" = 1.9e-16 rad, absorbed by sinCosInterval ABS_ERR 4e-15)

measurements.name: Clenshaw roundoff bound, derivative exactness, record-boundary handling
measurements.method: S/enclosures/clenshaw-bound2.mjs: fixed-point BigInt (2^300) exact evaluation, 3,102 evaluations over n in {4..64}, five coefficient families, 11 taus incl. +-1, 1-1e-12, 1+ulp, -1-ulp; S/enclosures/boundary.mjs: synthetic pack with non-integer initEt/intervalSec, one-ulp probes at every record edge
measurements.result: worst error/allowance 6.35e-2; sum|d_k| understated by <= 6.98e-17 relative; max|b_k|/sum|c| = (n-1)/2 exactly for n = 8,20,32,64; record selection correct at all 19 probes, tau = -1.0000000000000002 at 6 of 7 record starts, last inclusive end accepted (tau 0.9999999999999983), one ulp past refused, plain floor() wrong at 3 of 10 probes

swissGap.exceedPath: Add the Shapiro term (<= ~2e-4 s, < 1e-7") for completeness and put the light-time bound on every pointwise result

swissGap.swiss: FLG_SPEED, consistent with the apparent chain

Compute ayanamsas from the same precession chain (mean equinox of date to a fixed epoch) so the offset shares the frame's bound

swissGap.zodiacs: Proven enclosures of the pack polynomial inside the search modes (sound in every family tested; padding justified by slack in three places); nothing on the pointwise apparent() and the pack's proven fit bound excluded from results
